title.en: Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21 - Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang
title.raw: 卷六十九 唐書45: 列傳21 張憲 王正言 胡裝 崔貽孫 孟鵠 孫岳 張延朗 劉延皓 劉延朗 Volume 69 Book of Later Tang 45: Biographies 21 - Zhang Xian, Wang Zhengyan, Hu Zhuang, Cui Yisun, Meng Hu, Sun Yue, Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang

sentences.zh: 張憲，字允中，晉陽人，世以軍功為牙校。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian, whose courtesy name was Yunzhong, was a native of Jinyang; for generations his family had held yabing military staff posts through martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, courtesy name Yunzhong, came from Jinyang; his family had for generations earned yabing staff appointments through military service.

sentences.zh: 憲始童丱，喜儒學，勵志橫經，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: From childhood Xian loved Confucian learning, resolved to master the classics horizontally across the canon, and would not rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xian loved the Confucian classics and set himself to master them, studying without pause by day or night.

sentences.zh: 太原地雄邊服，人多尚武，恥於學業，惟憲與里人藥縱之精力遊學，弱冠盡通諸經，尤精《左傳》。

translations.literal: Taiyuan lay in a powerful frontier region; men mostly prized martial arts and were ashamed of scholarly pursuits. Only Xian and a townsman, Yao Zongzhi, threw their full energy into travel and study; by weak-crown age he had mastered all the classics and was especially expert in the 《Zuo Commentary》.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was a strong frontier district where men favored arms and looked down on book learning; only Xian and a neighbor, Yao Zongzhi, threw themselves into study abroad with all their strength. By twenty he had mastered every classic and knew the 《Zuo Commentary》 especially well.

sentences.zh: 嘗袖行所業，謁判官李襲吉，一見欣歎。

translations.literal: Once he tucked his recent compositions in his sleeve and called on the magistrate's aide Li Xiji; at first sight Xiji exclaimed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He once carried his latest writings in his sleeve to visit the magistrate's aide Li Xiji, who at first sight cried out in delight.

sentences.zh: 既辭，謂憲曰：「子勉之，將來必成佳器。

translations.literal: When he was taking leave, he said to Xian, "You must exert yourself—you are sure to become a fine vessel in the future.
translations.idiomatic: As Xian was leaving, he told him, "Apply yourself—you are bound to become a man of real promise.

sentences.zh: 」石州刺史楊守業喜聚書，以家書示之，聞見日博。

translations.literal: " The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, loved to gather books and showed him his family library, so his knowledge and experience grew broader day by day.
translations.idiomatic: " The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, was a collector of books and let him read his family library, so Xian's learning widened steadily.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為行軍司馬，廣延髦俊，素知憲名，令朱守殷齎書幣延之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong served as expedition marshal he widely sought outstanding talents, already knew Xian's name, and had Zhu Shouyin bring letters and gifts to invite him.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong was expedition marshal he sought out eminent men far and wide; knowing Xian's reputation, he sent Zhu Shouyin with letters and gifts to summon him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，釋褐交城令，秩滿，莊宗嗣世，補太原府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left the cloth and became magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne and he was appointed recorder of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he took his first office as magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended and Zhuangzong came to the throne, he was made recorder of the Jin prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 時霸府初開，幕客馬鬱、王緘，燕中名士，盡與之遊。

translations.literal: When the hegemon's headquarters first opened, his staff advisers Ma Yu and Wang Jian, celebrated men of Yan, all associated with him in study and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: As the princely headquarters first opened, staff advisers Ma Yu and Wang Jian—famous scholars of Yan—all became his companions.

sentences.zh: 十二年，莊宗平河朔，念藩邸之舊，征赴行台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei; mindful of his old comrades from the princely establishment, he summoned Xian to the field secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after Zhuangzong pacified Hebei, he recalled his old friends from the princely household and summoned Xian to the field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授監察，賜緋，署魏博推官，自是恒簪筆扈從。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was given the post of censor, granted crimson regalia, and made pushing officer for Weibo; from then on he constantly held the writing brush and followed in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made a censor, given crimson robes, and appointed pushing officer for Weibo; thereafter he always carried the brush and attended the ruler.

sentences.zh: 十五年，王師戰胡柳，周德威軍不利，憲與同列奔馬北渡；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year when the imperial army fought at Huliu, Zhou Dewei's army fared badly; Xian and his colleagues fled on horseback to cross north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's force was beaten, and Xian and his fellows galloped north to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 梁軍急追，殆將不濟。

translations.literal: The Liang army pressed hard in pursuit and they were nearly unable to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang troops pressed close behind, and they were almost unable to get across.

sentences.zh: 至晚渡河，人皆陷水而沒，憲與從子朗履冰而行；

translations.literal: By evening they forded the river; men all sank into the water and drowned, but Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed at dusk; most men fell into the water and drowned, but Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice.

sentences.zh: 將及岸，冰陷，朗泣，以馬箠引之，憲曰：「吾兒去矣，勿使俱陷。

translations.literal: As they neared the bank the ice gave way; Lang wept and used his riding crop to pull him; Xian said, "My boy, let go—do not let us both fall in.
translations.idiomatic: Near the bank the ice broke; Lang wept and pulled him with his riding crop. Xian said, "Let go, my boy—do not let us both go under.

sentences.zh: 」朗曰：「忍季父如此，俱死無恨。

translations.literal: " Lang said, "To endure my uncle's plight like this—we can die together without regret.
translations.idiomatic: " Lang said, "To see my uncle suffer this and not die with you—I could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 」朗偃伏引箠，憲躍身而出。

translations.literal: " Lang lay prostrate pulling with the crop; Xian leaped out bodily.
translations.idiomatic: " Lang lay flat and kept pulling with the crop while Xian sprang clear.

sentences.zh: 是夜，莊宗令於軍中求憲，或曰：「與王緘俱歿矣！

translations.literal: That night Zhuangzong ordered the army to search for Xian; some said, "He and Wang Jian have both perished!
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhuangzong had the army search for Xian; some said, "He and Wang Jian are both dead!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗垂涕求屍，數日，聞其免也，遣使慰勞。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong shed tears and sought their bodies; several days later when he heard Xian had survived he sent messengers to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong wept and asked for their bodies; days later, hearing Xian had escaped, he sent envoys to comfort and reward him.

sentences.zh: 尋改掌書記、水部郎中，賜金紫，曆魏博觀察判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was made chief secretary and director of the water bureau, granted gold and purple, and served successively as observing secretary for Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief secretary and director of the Water Bureau, given gold and purple insignia, and served as observing secretary for Weibo.

sentences.zh: 從討張文禮，鎮州平，授魏、博、鎮、冀十郡觀察判官，改考功郎中，兼御史中丞，權鎮州留事。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Zhang Wenli, when Zhen Prefecture was pacified he was made observing secretary for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director of the merit office and concurrently vice censor-in-chief, acting as regent for Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Zhang Wenli, after Zhen Prefecture was pacified he was made observing secretary for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then director of the Merit Office and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with acting charge of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，詔還魏都，授尚書工部侍郎，充租庸使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, an edict summoned him back to the Wei capital and appointed him vice minister of works, serving as commissioner for land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne, an edict recalled him to the Wei capital and made him vice minister of works and commissioner for land tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 八月，改刑部侍郎，判吏部銓，兼太清宮副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was changed to vice minister of punishments, adjudicating the board of personnel selections, and concurrently deputy commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, put in charge of personnel selection, and made deputy commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遷洛陽，以憲檢校吏部尚書、興唐尹、東京副留守，知留守事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong moved the capital to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, Xingtang prefect, and deputy metropolitan commandant at the eastern capital, in charge of metropolitan defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong moved the capital to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, and deputy eastern-capital commandant in charge of metropolitan affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲學識優深，尤精吏道，剖析聽斷，人不敢欺。

translations.literal: Xian's learning was profound and superior, and he was especially expert in the ways of official administration; in analyzing cases and hearing judgments no one dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's learning ran deep, and he knew official practice especially well; in hearing cases and weighing evidence no one dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 三年春，車駕幸鄴，時易定王都來朝，宴於行宮，將擊鞠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the imperial carriage visited Ye; at that time the king of Yiding came to court, and at the traveling palace a banquet was held with cuju to be played.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor went to Ye; the king of Yiding had come to court, and at the traveling palace a feast was held before a game of cuju.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗行即位之禮，卜鞠場吉，因築壇於其間，至是詔毀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong performed the accession rites, divination on the cuju ground proved auspicious, so an altar was built there; now an edict ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong had first performed his accession rites, divination on the cuju field had been favorable, so an altar was built there; now he ordered it torn down.

sentences.zh: 憲奏曰：「即位壇是陛下祭接天神受命之所，自風燥雨濡之外，不可輒毀，亦不可修。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized, "The accession altar is where Your Majesty sacrificed to receive Heaven's mandate; apart from damage by wind-dryness or rain-soaking, it must not be rashly destroyed, nor rashly repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Xian submitted, "The accession altar is where Your Majesty received Heaven's mandate in sacrifice; apart from weathering, it must neither be casually destroyed nor casually restored.

sentences.zh: 魏繁陽之壇，漢汜水之墠，到今猶有兆象。

translations.literal: The altar of Fanyang in Wei and the mound at Sishui in Han—even to the present there remain traces and signs.
translations.idiomatic: The altar at Fanyang under Wei and the mound at Sishui under Han still show their traces today.

sentences.zh: 存而不毀，古之道也。

translations.literal: To preserve and not destroy—this is the way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: To keep them and not destroy them—that is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 」即命治之於宮西。

translations.literal: " He was immediately ordered to restore it west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He was told at once to restore it west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 數日，未成。

translations.literal: Several days passed and it was not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the work was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 會憲以公事獲謫，閣門待罪，上怒，戒有司速治行宮之庭，礙事者畢去，竟毀即位壇。

translations.literal: It happened that Xian was demoted for an official matter and waited at the gate for punishment; the emperor was angry and warned the offices to quickly prepare the traveling palace courtyard, removing all obstructions, and in the end the accession altar was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xian was demoted on an official charge and waited at the gate to answer for it; the emperor was angry and told the offices to clear the traveling palace court at once, removing everything in the way, and the accession altar was destroyed after all.

sentences.zh: 憲私謂郭崇韜曰：「不祥之甚，忽其本也。」

translations.literal: Xian privately told Guo Chongtao, "This is most inauspicious—neglecting the root."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said privately to Guo Chongtao, "This is a grave ill omen—they are forgetting their foundation."

sentences.zh: 秋，崇韜將兵征蜀，以手書告憲曰：「允中避事久矣，餘受命西征，已奏還公黃閣。

translations.literal: In autumn Chongtao was leading troops to conquer Shu and wrote Xian by hand, "Yunzhong has long avoided office; I have received orders for the western campaign and have already memorialized to return you to the Yellow Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Chongtao marched against Shu and wrote Xian by hand: "Yunzhong, you have long stayed out of office; I have been ordered west and have already asked to bring you back to the Yellow Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 」憲報曰：「庖人之代屍祝，所謂非吾事也。

translations.literal: " Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the invocator at sacrifice—this is what is called 'not my affair.'
translations.idiomatic: " Xian replied, "For the cook to stand in for the sacrificer—that is what people call 'not my business.'

sentences.zh: 」時樞密承旨段徊當權任事，以憲從龍舊望，不欲憲在朝廷。

translations.literal: " At that time the Secretariat commissioner Duan Hui held power and conducted affairs; because of Xian's old prestige as a follower of the dragon, he did not want Xian at court.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Duan Hui of the Secretariat held power; because of Xian's standing as an old companion of the throne, he did not want Xian at court.

sentences.zh: 會孟知祥鎮蜀川，選北京留守，徊揚言曰：「北門，國家根本，非重德不可輕授；

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang was garrisoning Shu, they were choosing a northern-capital regent; Hui proclaimed publicly, "The northern gate is the state's foundation—it cannot be lightly entrusted except to a man of weighty virtue;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang was posted to Shu, they had to choose a northern-capital regent; Hui declared openly, "The northern gate is the root of the state and cannot be given lightly except to a man of great weight;

sentences.zh: 今之取才，非憲不可。

translations.literal: for the choice of talent today, none but Xian will do.
translations.idiomatic: for this choice there is no one but Xian.

sentences.zh: 」趨時者因附徊勢，巧中傷之。

translations.literal: " Men who courted the times attached themselves to Hui's power and artfully slandered Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who trimmed to the moment clung to Hui's influence and found clever ways to wound him.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「憲有相業，然國祚中興，宰相在天子麵前，得失可以改作；

translations.literal: He also said, "Xian has the makings of a chief minister, yet as the dynasty's fortune is reviving, a chancellor before the Son of Heaven can have his errors corrected;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xian has the talent of a chief minister, but in this revival of the dynasty a chancellor stands before the Son of Heaven and his mistakes can be corrected;

sentences.zh: 一方之事，製在一人，惟北面事重。

translations.literal: affairs of one region are controlled by a single man—only the northern-front matter is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: affairs of a whole region rest in one man's hands, and only the northern command matters.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，授憲銀青光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、太原尹、北京留守，知府事。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month Xian was given silver-blue gleam grand master, acting minister of personnel, Taiyuan prefect, and northern-capital regent, administering prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month Xian was made Silver-Blue Gleam Grand Master, acting minister of personnel, prefect of Taiyuan, and northern-capital regent in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮入魏州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili entered Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili marched into Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時憲家屬在魏，關東俶擾，在禮善待其家，遣人齎書至太原誘憲。

translations.literal: At that time Xian's family were in Wei; the east of the passes was in turmoil; Zaili treated his family well and sent a man bearing a letter to Taiyuan to entice Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's family were then in Wei; the east was in uproar; Zaili treated them kindly and sent a messenger with a letter to Taiyuan to win Xian over.

sentences.zh: 憲斬其使，書不發函而奏。

translations.literal: Xian beheaded the envoy, did not open the letter's seal, and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Xian executed the envoy, left the letter unopened, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗為兵眾所劫，諸軍離散，地遠不知事實，或謂憲曰：「蜀軍未至，洛陽窘急，總管又失兵權，製在諸軍之手，又聞河朔推戴，事若實然，或可濟否？

translations.literal: Soon afterward Mingzong was seized by the troops, the armies scattered, and the region was far away so the facts were unknown; some said to Xian, "The Shu army has not arrived, Luoyang is in dire straits, the commander-in-chief has also lost military authority, control is in the armies' hands, and we hear Hebei is pushing someone for enthronement—if matters are truly so, might there still be a way through?
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mingzong was seized by the troops and the armies broke apart; far from the capital no one knew the truth, and some asked Xian, "The Shu army has not come, Luoyang is desperate, the commander has lost his soldiers, power lies with the armies, and we hear Hebei is raising a ruler—if things are really like that, is there still hope?

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「治亂之機，間不容發，以愚所斷，事未可知。

translations.literal: " Xian said, "The hinge of order and chaos admits no gap; by my dull judgment the outcome cannot yet be known.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "The turn between order and chaos allows no delay; by my poor reading, nothing is certain yet.

sentences.zh: 愚聞藥縱之言，總管德量仁厚，素得士心，餘勿多言，誌此而已。

translations.literal: I have heard Yao Zong's words: the commander-in-chief's virtue and magnanimity are humane and generous, and he has long won the hearts of officers—say no more; record only this.
translations.idiomatic: I recall what Yao Zong said: the commander is humane and generous and has long held the soldiers' hearts. Say no more—remember only that.

sentences.zh: 」四月五日，李存渥自洛陽至，口傳莊宗命，並無書詔，惟云天子授以隻箭，傳之為信。

translations.literal: " On the fifth day of the fourth month Li Cunwo came from Luoyang, orally conveying Zhuangzong's command; there was no written edict—only that the Son of Heaven had given a single arrow as token to be passed along as proof.
translations.idiomatic: " On the fifth of the fourth month Li Cunwo arrived from Luoyang with Zhuangzong's orders by word of mouth and no written edict—only that the emperor had given a single arrow as proof to pass on.

sentences.zh: 眾心惑之，時事莫測。

translations.literal: The hearts of the crowd were unsettled and the times could not be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Men were uncertain, and no one could tell how events would turn.

sentences.zh: 左右獻畫曰：「存渥所乘馬，已戢其飾，復召人謀事，必行陰禍，因欲據城。

translations.literal: Those at his side offered a plan, saying, "The horse Cunwo rides has already had its trappings removed; he has again summoned men to plot affairs—he is sure to work hidden harm and thereby seize the city.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged a plan: "Cunwo's horse already has its trappings stripped off; he is summoning men again to plot—he means treachery and to seize the city.

sentences.zh: 寧我負人，宜早為之所，但戮呂、鄭二宦，且係存渥，徐觀其變，事萬全矣。

translations.literal: Better that I wrong others than be wronged—act early; only kill the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, and also detain Cunwo, then watch the changes slowly—the affair will be wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: Better we wrong others than be wronged ourselves—strike first; kill only the two eunuchs Lü and Zheng, hold Cunwo, and watch how things develop—the plan will be safe.

sentences.zh: 」憲良久曰：「吾本書生，無軍功而致身及此，一旦自布衣而紆金紫，向來仕宦非出他門，此畫非吾心也。

translations.literal: " Xian was silent a long while and said, "I was originally a scholar; without military merit I have reached this station, and in a single day rose from plain cloth to gold and purple. My career has never come through another's gate—this plan is not in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was silent a long time and said, "I was only a scholar; without battle merit I have come this far, from common cloth to gold and purple in a day. My whole career has never passed through another man's door—this plan is not mine.

sentences.zh: 事苟不濟，以身徇義。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, I will give my body to uphold righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, I will give my life for what is right."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·張昭傳》：昭勸憲奉表明宗以勸進，憲曰：「吾書生也，天子委以保厘之任，吾豈苟生者乎！

translations.literal: (The 《Eastern Capital Epitome · Biography of Zhang Zhao》: Zhao urged Xian to submit a memorial to Mingzong to advance him to the throne; Xian said, "I am a scholar; the Son of Heaven entrusted me with the charge of guarding and comforting the realm—how could I cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Eastern Capital Epitome · Biography of Zhang Zhao》: Zhao urged Xian to memorialize Mingzong to advance him to the throne. Xian said, "I am a scholar; the Son of Heaven gave me charge of the northern capital—how could I cling to life!

sentences.zh: 」昭曰：「此古之大節，公能行之，忠臣也。

translations.literal: " Zhao said, "This is the great integrity of antiquity; if the lord can carry it out, he is a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao said, "That is the great integrity of the ancients; if you can do it, you are a true loyalist.

sentences.zh: 」憲既死，論者以昭能成憲之節。）〉

translations.literal: " After Xian died, commentators held that Zhao had helped Xian fulfill his integrity.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " After Xian's death, commentators said Zhao had helped him keep his integrity.)〉

sentences.zh: 翌日，符彥超誅呂、鄭，軍城大亂，燔剽達曙。

translations.literal: The next day Fu Yanchao killed Lü and Zheng; the army city fell into great disorder, with burning and plunder until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fu Yanchao killed Lü and Zheng; the garrison city erupted in chaos, with fire and looting until dawn.

sentences.zh: 憲初聞有變，出奔沂州。

translations.literal: When Xian first heard of the upheaval he fled toward Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian first heard of the turmoil he fled toward Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而有司糾其委城之罪，四月二十四日，賜死於晉陽之千佛院。

translations.literal: Soon the offices impeached him for the crime of abandoning the city; on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month he was granted death at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the authorities charged him with abandoning the city; on the twenty-fourth of the fourth month he was ordered to die at the Thousand Buddha Monastery in Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 幼子凝隨父走，亦為收者加害。

translations.literal: His young son Ning followed his father in flight and was also harmed by those who seized them.
translations.idiomatic: His young son Ning fled with him and was killed by those who captured them.

sentences.zh: 明宗郊禮大赦，有司請昭雪，從之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong performed the suburban rites and proclaimed a great amnesty, the offices requested that Xian be cleared, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong's suburban sacrifice and great amnesty the offices asked that Xian be cleared, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 憲沈靜寡欲，喜聚圖書，家書五千卷，視事之餘，手自刊校。

translations.literal: Xian was calm and quiet, with few desires; he loved to gather books and had five thousand volumes in his family library; in the intervals of official business he personally collated and proofread them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was calm and frugal, loved books, and kept five thousand volumes at home; when office work allowed, he collated them with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，不飲酒，賓僚宴語，但論文嘯詠而已，士友重之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at the zither and did not drink wine; at banquets with guests and staff he spoke only of literature and chanting poetry, and scholar-friends held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither well and did not drink; at feasts with colleagues he spoke only of literature and poetry, and men of learning respected him.

sentences.zh: 憲長子守素，仕晉，位至尚書。

translations.literal: Xian's eldest son Shousu served Jin and rose to minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's eldest son Shousu served the Jin state and rose to minister.

sentences.zh: 王正言，鄆州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan was a native of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan came from Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父誌，濟陰令。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was magistrate of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been magistrate of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 正言早孤貧，從沙門學，工詩，密州刺史賀德倫令歸俗，署郡職。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was orphaned early and poor; he studied under Buddhist monks and was skilled at poetry; the prefect of Mi, He Delun, had him return to lay life and appointed him to a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan lost his father young and was poor; he studied with Buddhist monks and wrote poetry well; He Delun, prefect of Mi, had him leave the clergy and gave him a post in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德倫鎮青州，表為推官；

translations.literal: When Delun was garrisoned at Qing Prefecture he recommended him as pushing officer;
translations.idiomatic: When Delun was posted to Qing Prefecture he recommended him as pushing officer;

sentences.zh: 移鎮魏州，改觀察判官。

translations.literal: when he moved his garrison to Wei Prefecture, he was changed to observing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: and when Delun moved to Wei Prefecture, Zhengyan became observing secretary.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定魏博，正言仍舊職任，小心端慎，與物無競。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan kept his old post; he was careful, upright, and cautious, and did not compete with others.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Weibo, Zhengyan kept his post; he was careful and unassuming and did not contend with others.

sentences.zh: 嘗為同職司空頲所淩，正言降心下之。

translations.literal: Once he was bullied by a colleague of the same rank, Sikong Hui; Zhengyan lowered his heart and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was once bullied by a fellow officer, Sikong Hui, but Zhengyan humbled himself and yielded.

sentences.zh: 頲誅，代為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Hui was executed, he replaced him as military-governor secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was executed, Zhengyan replaced him as military-governor secretary.

sentences.zh: 同光初，守戶部尚書、興唐尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he held minister of revenue and was Xingtang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tongguang era he was minister of revenue and prefect of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙為租庸副使，常畏張憲挺特，不欲其領使，乃白郭崇韜留憲於魏州，請宰相豆盧革判租庸。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian was deputy commissioner for land tax and corvée and often feared Zhang Xian's upright firmness; he did not want Xian to head the commission, so he told Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Wei Prefecture and asked the chancellor Dou Luge to adjudicate land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian was then deputy commissioner for land tax and corvée and feared Zhang Xian's stiff integrity; not wanting Xian to head the office, he urged Guo Chongtao to keep Xian at Wei and asked the chancellor Dou Luge to run land tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以盧質代之。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Zhi was again made to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu Zhi replaced Dou in the role.

sentences.zh: 孔謙白云：「錢穀重務，宰相事多，簿籍留滯。

translations.literal: Kong Qian told Chongtao, "Revenue and grain are weighty affairs; the chancellor has many duties and the ledgers lag.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian told Chongtao, "Money and grain are vital; the chancellor has too much else to do, and the books pile up.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「盧質判二日，便借官錢，皆不可任。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Lu Zhi, after adjudicating two days, at once borrowed official funds—none of them can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Lu Zhi borrowed official money after only two days on the job—none of them are fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 」意謂崇韜必令己代其任，時物議未允而止，謙沮喪久之。

translations.literal: " He meant that Chongtao would surely have him replace the post; public opinion at the time did not agree and it stopped, and Qian was dejected for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " He expected Chongtao to put him in charge, but public opinion would not allow it and the plan stopped; Qian was discouraged for a long while.

sentences.zh: 李紹宏曰：「邦計國本，時號怨府，非張憲不稱職。

translations.literal: Li Shaohong said, "State revenue is the nation's foundation and is at the time called the 'house of grievance'—none but Zhang Xian is fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong said, "State finance is the root of the realm and is called the house of complaints—only Zhang Xian is fit for the job.

sentences.zh: 」即日征之。

translations.literal: " That same day Xian was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was summoned the same day.

sentences.zh: 孔謙、段徊白崇韜曰：「邦計雖重，在侍中眼前，但得一人為使即可。

translations.literal: Kong Qian and Duan Hui told Chongtao, "Though state revenue is weighty, it is before the vice director's eyes—only one man need serve as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian and Duan Hui told Chongtao, "Finance is important, but it is right before the vice director—any one man can run it.

sentences.zh: 魏博六州戶口，天下之半，王正言操守有餘，智力不足，若朝廷任使，庶幾與人共事；

translations.literal: The six prefectures of Weibo hold half the empire's households; Wang Zhengyan has integrity in surplus but intellect and power insufficient—if the court employs him, he might barely work with others;
translations.idiomatic: Weibo's six prefectures hold half the empire's population; Wang Zhengyan has integrity to spare but not enough wit—at court he might manage as someone's subordinate;

sentences.zh: 若專製方隅，未見其可。

translations.literal: if given sole control of a region, one does not yet see that he can do it.
translations.idiomatic: but left alone over a region, he would not do.

sentences.zh: 張憲才器兼濟，宜以委之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian's talent and capacity are both complete—he should be entrusted with it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian has both talent and capacity and should be given the post.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜即奏憲留守魏州，征王正言為租庸使。

translations.literal: " Chongtao at once memorialized to keep Xian as regent at Wei Prefecture and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner for land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongtao then had Xian stay as regent at Wei and summoned Wang Zhengyan as commissioner for land tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 正言在職，主諾而已，權柄出於孔謙。

translations.literal: In office Zhengyan merely assented; real power lay with Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In office Zhengyan only nodded assent; Kong Qian held the real power.

sentences.zh: 正言不耐繁浩，簿領縱橫，觸事遺忘，物論以為不可，即以孔謙代之，正言守禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhengyan could not endure the complexity; ledgers lay crisscrossed and he forgot matters at every turn; public opinion held him unfit, so Kong Qian replaced him and Zhengyan kept only minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan could not bear the tangle of paperwork and forgot things at every turn; opinion said he was unfit, Kong Qian replaced him, and Zhengyan was left as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，代張憲為興唐尹，留守鄴都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as Xingtang prefect and regent at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he replaced Zhang Xian as prefect of Xingtang and regent at Ye.

sentences.zh: 時武德使史彥瓊，監守鄴都，廩帑出納，兵馬製置，皆出彥瓊，將佐官吏，頤指氣使，正言不能以道禦之，但趑趄聽命。

translations.literal: At that time the Martial Virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong supervised and guarded Ye; disbursement of granaries and treasuries and disposition of troops and horses all came from Yanqiong; generals, aides, and officials he commanded with chin and breath—Zhengyan could not restrain him by the Way but only shrank and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Virtue commissioner Shi Yanqiong then controlled Ye—grain, funds, troops, and horses all passed through him, and officers and clerks took orders from his gesture; Zhengyan could not check him by principle and only shrank back and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至是，貝州戍兵亂，入魏州，彥瓊望風敗走，亂兵剽劫坊市。

translations.literal: At this time the garrison troops of Bei Prefecture mutinied and entered Wei Prefecture; Yanqiong fled at the sight of the wind; the mutinous troops plundered the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Bei garrison mutinied and marched into Wei; Yanqiong fled at the first alarm; the mutineers looted the streets.

sentences.zh: 正言促召書吏寫奏章，家人曰：「賊已殺人縱火，都城已陷，何奏之有。

translations.literal: Zhengyan urgently summoned clerks to draft a memorial; his household said, "The rebels have already killed and set fires—the capital is fallen; what memorial is there to write."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan hurried clerks to draft a memorial; his family said, "The rebels are killing and burning—the capital is lost; what is there to memorialize."

sentences.zh: 」是日，正言引諸僚佐謁趙在禮，

translations.literal: " That day Zhengyan led all his staff aides to call on Zhao Zaili,
translations.idiomatic: " That day Zhengyan led his staff to call on Zhao Zaili,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：正言索馬，不能得，乃帥僚佐步出府門謁在禮。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Zhengyan sought a horse but could not obtain one, so he led his staff on foot out the prefectural gate to call on Zaili.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Zhengyan asked for a horse and could not get one, so he led his staff on foot out the gate to visit Zaili.)〉

sentences.zh: 望塵再拜請罪。

translations.literal: seeing the dust he bowed twice and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: bowed twice in the dust and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 在禮曰：「尚書重德，勿自卑屈，餘受國恩，與尚書共事，但思歸之眾，倉卒見迫耳。

translations.literal: Zaili said, "The minister is a man of weighty virtue—do not humble yourself; I have received the state's grace and served with the minister; it is only that the crowd longing to return home pressed me in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili said, "Minister, you are a man of weight—do not abase yourself; I owe the state and have served with you; the men only wanted to go home and forced my hand in haste.

sentences.zh: 」因拜正言，厚加慰撫。

translations.literal: " He then bowed to Zhengyan and comforted him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed to Zhengyan in return and comforted him warmly.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，正言求為平盧軍行軍司馬，因以授之，竟卒於任。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zhengyan requested to be expedition marshal of the Pinglu army and was appointed; he died in office at last.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne, Zhengyan asked to be expedition marshal of Pinglu and received the post; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 胡裝，禮部尚書曾之孫。

translations.literal: Hu Zhuang was grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhuang was a grandson of Zeng, former minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 汴將楊師厚之鎮魏州，裝與副使李嗣業有舊，因往依之，薦授貴鄉令。

translations.literal: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was garrisoned at Wei Prefecture, Zhuang had old ties with vice commissioner Li Siye and went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang general Yang Shihou held Wei Prefecture, Zhuang, who knew vice commissioner Li Siye, went to join him and was recommended as magistrate of Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 及張彥之亂，嗣業遇害，裝罷秩，客於魏州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yan's rebellion came, Siye was killed; Zhuang lost his post and lodged as a guest in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan rebelled, Siye was killed; Zhuang lost his office and stayed on in Wei as a guest.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初至，裝謁見，求假官，司空頲以其居官貪濁，不得調者久之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional post; Sikong Hui, because he had been corrupt in office, long kept him from appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang paid his respects and asked for a post; Sikong Hui, citing his corruption in office, long blocked his appointment.

sentences.zh: 十三年，莊宗還太原，裝候於離亭；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan, Zhuang waited at the farewell pavilion;

sentences.zh: 謁者不內，乃排闥而入，曰：「臣本朝公卿子孫，從兵至此。

translations.literal: the usher would not admit him, so he pushed through the door and entered, saying, "Your servant is a descendant of this dynasty's dukes and ministers and has followed the army to this place.
translations.idiomatic: the usher would not let him in, so he forced the door and said, "I am a descendant of Tang ministers and have followed the army here.

sentences.zh: 殿下比襲唐祚，勤求英俊，以壯霸圖。

translations.literal: Your Highness has lately assumed Tang's mandate and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen the hegemonic design.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has lately taken up Tang's mandate and seeks able men to strengthen your cause.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不才，比於進九九，納豎刁、頭須，亦所庶幾。

translations.literal: Though your servant lacks talent, compared with presenting Jiu Jiu, or taking in Shu Diao and Guan Zhong, it is still within hope.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack talent, compared with presenting Jiu Jiu or taking in Shu Diao and Guan Zhong, I am not wholly unworthy.

sentences.zh: 而羈旅累年，執事者不垂顧錄，臣不能赴海觸樹，走胡適越，今日歸死於殿下也！

translations.literal: Yet I have been a wanderer for years and those in charge have not shown regard; your servant cannot go to sea and strike a tree, flee to the Hu or hurry to Yue—today I return to die before Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have wandered for years without notice from those in charge; I cannot flee abroad or go elsewhere—today I come to die before Your Highness!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗愕然曰：「孤未之知，何至如是！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong was startled and said, "I did not know—how could it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong was astonished and said, "I did not know it had come to this!

sentences.zh: 」賜酒食慰遣之，謂郭崇韜曰：「便與擬議。

translations.literal: " He gave wine and food to comfort and send him off, and told Guo Chongtao, "Go ahead and draft a proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him food and wine and told Guo Chongtao, "Draw up a proposal for him.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，署館驛巡官。

translations.literal: " That year he was appointed touring officer of post stations.
translations.idiomatic: " That year he was made touring officer of the post stations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授監察御史裏行，遷節度巡官，賜緋魚袋；

translations.literal: Before long he was given acting investigating censor, promoted to circuit touring officer, and granted crimson fish tally;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting investigating censor, then circuit touring officer, with a crimson fish tally;

sentences.zh: 尋曆推官、檢校員外郎。

translations.literal: soon he served successively as pushing officer and acting vice director.
translations.idiomatic: and soon served as pushing officer and acting vice director.

sentences.zh: 裝學書無師法，工詩非作者，僻於題壁，所至宮亭寺觀，必書爵裏，人或譏之，不以為愧。

translations.literal: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper method, was skilled at poetry but not a true author, and was eccentric in writing on walls—wherever he went to palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he would inscribe rank and native place; people sometimes mocked him, but he was not ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang learned calligraphy without real training, wrote verse without being a poet, and had a habit of inscribing walls—at every shrine and pavilion he wrote his rank and home; people mocked him, but he was unashamed.

sentences.zh: 時四鎮幕賓皆金紫，裝獨恥銀艾。

translations.literal: At the time staff guests of the four circuits all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and green.
translations.idiomatic: Staff guests of the four circuits all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of his silver and green insignia.

sentences.zh: 十七年，莊宗自魏州之德勝，與賓僚城樓餞別，既而群僚離席，裝獨留，獻詩三篇，意在章服。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, as Zhuangzong went from Wei Prefecture to Desheng, he parted from guests and staff on the city tower; when the group had left their seats Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his aim being regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong left Wei for Desheng and bid farewell to his staff on the city tower; when the others left, Zhuang alone stayed and offered three poems, angling for higher regalia.

sentences.zh: 莊宗舉大鍾屬裝曰：「員外能釂此乎？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Can the vice director drain this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raised a great goblet and said to Zhuang, "Can you drain this, Vice Director?

sentences.zh: 」裝飲酒素少，略無難色，為之一舉而釂，莊宗即解紫袍賜之。

translations.literal: " Zhuang ordinarily drank little, but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one lift; Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuang drank little as a rule, but showed no hesitation, downed it in one draft, and Zhuangzong at once gave him his purple robe.

sentences.zh: 同光初，以裝為給事中，從幸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant within the palace gates and followed the emperor to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tongguang he was made palace attendant and followed the court to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時連年大水，百官多窘，裝求為襄州副使。

translations.literal: At the time floods came year after year and many officials were straitened; Zhuang sought to be vice commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Floods came year after year and many officials were hard pressed; Zhuang asked to be vice commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，洛陽變擾，節度使劉訓以私忿族裝，誣奏雲裝欲謀亂，人士冤之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Luoyang was thrown into turmoil, the military governor Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended rebellion; gentlemen held it a grievous wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Luoyang was in turmoil, military governor Liu Xun, from private spite, wiped out Zhuang's clan and falsely accused him of plotting rebellion; men of standing thought it a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 崔貽孫，

translations.literal: Cui Yisun,
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yisun,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·宰相世係表》：貽孫字伯垂。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang · Genealogical Tables of Chancellors》: Yisun's courtesy name was Bochui.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang · Genealogical Tables of Chancellors》: Yisun's courtesy name was Bochui.)〉

sentences.zh: 祖元亮，左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanliang was left attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanliang had been left attendant cavalier.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《世係表》：元亮，字晦孫，虢州刺史。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Genealogical Tables》: Yuanliang, courtesy name Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Genealogical Tables》: Yuanliang, courtesy name Huisun, was prefect of Guo.)〉

sentences.zh: 父芻言，潞州判官。

translations.literal: His father Chuyan was secretary of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuyan had been secretary of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以門族登進士第，以監察升朝，曆清資美職。

translations.literal: Yisun by family standing passed the jinshi examination, rose to court by censor's post, and served in pure-capacity and fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun passed the jinshi through family standing, entered court as a censor, and held a series of prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 及為省郎，使於江南回，以橐裝營別墅於漢上之穀城，退居自奉。

translations.literal: When he was a ministry gentleman, returning from a mission to Jiangnan, he used his traveling funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a ministry officer, returning from a mission to the south, he used his travel funds to build a villa at Gucheng on the Han and retired there.

sentences.zh: 清江之上，綠竹遍野，狹徑濃密，維舟曲岸，人莫造焉，時人甚高之。

translations.literal: Above the clear river green bamboo spread over the fields; narrow paths lay thick and dense; he moored his boat on the winding bank where people did not venture—men of the time held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Green bamboo covered the clear river; narrow paths ran thick; he moored on a secluded bend where visitors rarely came, and contemporaries admired him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及李振貶均州，貽孫曲奉之。

translations.literal: When Li Zhen was demoted to Jun Prefecture, Yisun curried favor with him obsequiously.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhen was demoted to Jun Prefecture, Yisun fawned on him.

sentences.zh: 振入朝，貽孫累遷丞郎。

translations.literal: When Zhen entered court, Yisun was repeatedly promoted to director and gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen returned to court, Yisun rose steadily to director and gentleman posts.

sentences.zh: 同光初，除吏部侍郎，銓選疏謬，貶官塞地，馳驛至潞州，致書於府帥孔曰：「十五年穀城山裏，自謂逸人；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made vice minister of personnel; his selections were careless and absurd, he was demoted to a frontier post, and galloped by post horse to Lu Prefecture, writing to the prefect Kong, "For fifteen years in the Gucheng mountains I called myself a recluse;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tongguang he was made vice minister of personnel; his appointments were slipshod, he was demoted to the frontier, and rode post-haste to Lu, writing the prefect Kong: "For fifteen years in the Gucheng hills I called myself a recluse;

sentences.zh: 二千里沙塞途中，今為逐客。

translations.literal: on a two-thousand-li road through desert passes, I am now an expelled guest.
translations.idiomatic: now, two thousand li through the desert, I am an exile.

sentences.zh: 」以其年八十，奏留府下。

translations.literal: " Because he was eighty, a memorial asked that he be kept at the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: " Because he was eighty, he was allowed to remain at the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 明年，量移澤州司馬，遇赦還京。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred by degree to military aide of Ze Prefecture; on encountering an amnesty he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to military aide of Ze Prefecture; after an amnesty he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭玨以姻戚之分，復擬吏部侍郎，天官任重，昏耄罔知，後遷禮部尚書，致仕而卒。

translations.literal: The chancellor Zheng Jue, because of marriage ties, again proposed him as vice minister of personnel; the Heavenly Office's burden was heavy, and in senility he knew nothing; later he was moved to minister of rites, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zheng Jue, a relation by marriage, had him proposed again as vice minister of personnel; the post was weighty, but he was senile and unaware; later he was made minister of rites, retired, and died.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：崔貽孫年過八十，求進不休，囊橐之資，素有貯積，性好幹人，喜得小惠。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Idle Talk of Northern Dreams》: Cui Yisun passed eighty but never ceased seeking advancement; his purse and bags he had long stored up; by nature he loved to meddle with people and delighted in small favors.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Idle Talk of Northern Dreams》: Cui Yisun was past eighty but never stopped seeking promotion; he had long hoarded his funds; he loved to meddle and delighted in small favors.)〉

sentences.zh: 有子三人，自貽孫左降之後，各於舊業爭分其利，甘旨醫藥，莫有奉者。

translations.literal: He had three sons; after Yisun's demotion each contended over the profits of his old enterprises; for delicacies and medicine none provided.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons; after his demotion each fought over the profits of his old businesses, and none brought him food or medicine.

sentences.zh: 貽孫以書責之云：「生有明君宰相，死有天曹地府，吾雖考終，豈放汝耶！」

translations.literal: Yisun wrote to reprove them, saying, "In life there are enlightened rulers and chancellors; in death there are the heavenly bureau and the underworld—I may die in my bed, but will I let you go!"
translations.idiomatic: Yisun wrote to rebuke them: "In life there are enlightened rulers and chancellors; in death Heaven and the underworld keep accounts—I may die in my bed, but I will not let you off!"

sentences.zh: 孟鵠，魏州人。

translations.literal: Meng Hu was a native of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hu came from Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初定魏博，選幹吏以計兵賦，以鵠為度支孔目官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo, he chose capable officials to calculate troops and levies and made Hu revenue clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first pacified Weibo, he chose able men to reckon troops and taxes and made Hu a revenue clerk.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為邢洺節度使，每曲意承迎，明宗甚德之。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was military governor of Xing and Ming and at every turn curried favor; Mingzong was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was military governor of Xing and Ming and always courted favor; Mingzong thought well of him.

sentences.zh: 及孔謙專典軍賦，徵督苛急，明宗嘗切齒。

translations.literal: When Kong Qian monopolized military supplies and collections were harsh and urgent, Mingzong once gnashed his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Qian controlled military finance and collections grew harsh, Mingzong once gnashed his teeth in anger.

sentences.zh: 及即位，鵠自租庸勾官擢為客省副使、樞密承旨，遷三司副使，出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Hu was raised from land-tax checking clerk to vice commissioner of the guest bureau and Secretariat commissioner, moved to deputy commissioner of the three offices, and sent out as prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Hu rose from land-tax clerk to vice guest commissioner and Secretariat commissioner, then deputy three-offices commissioner, and was sent out as prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 會範延光再遷樞密，乃征鵠為三司使。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang was again moved to the Secretariat, Hu was summoned as commissioner of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang returned to the Secretariat, Hu was summoned as three-offices commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，鵠有計畫之能，及專掌邦賦，操割依違，名譽頓減。

translations.literal: At first Hu had planning ability, but once he solely managed state levies he sliced and wavered in his cuts, and his reputation suddenly fell.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hu had a gift for planning, but once he controlled state revenue he squeezed and wavered, and his reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 期年發疾，求外任，仍授許州節度使。

translations.literal: Within a year he fell ill, sought an outer post, and was still appointed military governor of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he fell ill, asked for an outside post, and was made military governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 謝恩退，帝目送之，顧為侍臣曰：「孟鵠掌三司幾年，得至方鎮？

translations.literal: After thanking him and taking leave, the emperor watched him go and turned to attendants, saying, "Meng Hu ran the three offices for how many years to reach a frontier command?
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew after giving thanks, the emperor watched him go and said to his attendants, "How many years did Meng Hu run the three offices to reach a frontier command?

sentences.zh: 」範延光奏曰：「鵠於同光世已為三司勾官，天成初為三司副使，出刺相州，入判三司又二年。

translations.literal: " Fan Yanguang submitted, "In the Tongguang era Hu was already a three-offices checking clerk; at the beginning of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner, went out as prefect of Xiang, and judged the three offices again for two years.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Yanguang replied, "In Tongguang he was already a three-offices clerk; at the start of Tiancheng he was deputy commissioner, went out to Xiang, and ran the three offices again for two years.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「鵠以幹事，遽至方鎮，爭不勉旃。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Hu, through busywork, suddenly reached a frontier command—how could he not strive harder?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Hu reached a frontier command through busywork alone—why should he not try harder?

sentences.zh: 」鵠與延光俱魏人，厚相結托，暨延光掌樞務，援引判三司，又致節鉞，明宗知之，故以此言譏之。

translations.literal: " Hu and Yanguang were both men of Wei and bound themselves closely; when Yanguang took charge of Secretariat affairs he pulled Hu in to judge the three offices and also secured a command baton—Mingzong knew this, and therefore spoke these words in mockery.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu and Yanguang were both from Wei and were close allies; when Yanguang took the Secretariat he pushed Hu into the three offices and a military command—Mingzong knew it, and his remark was meant as sarcasm.

sentences.zh: 到任未周歲，卒。

translations.literal: He had not completed a year in office when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before completing a year in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 孫嶽，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yue was a native of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yue came from Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 強幹有才用，曆府衛右職。

translations.literal: Forceful and capable, he served in right-hand posts of the guard and metropolitan offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was forceful and capable and held senior posts in the guard and metropolitan offices.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為潁耀二州刺史、閬州團練使，所至稱治，遷鳳州節度使。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he was prefect of Ying and Yao and training commissioner of Lang; wherever he went he was praised for good rule, and he was moved to military governor of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng he was prefect of Ying and Yao and training commissioner of Lang; wherever he went he was praised for good government, and he was made military governor of Feng.

sentences.zh: 受代歸京，秦王從榮欲以嶽為元帥府都押衙，事未行，馮贇舉為三司使，時預密謀。

translations.literal: When relieved and returned to the capital, Prince of Qin Congrong wished to make Yue chief military adjutant of the marshal's headquarters; the matter had not been carried out when Feng Yun recommended him as three-offices commissioner—at the time he took part in secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: On returning after his term, Prince Congrong of Qin wanted him as chief adjutant of the marshal's staff; before that happened Feng Yun recommended him as three-offices commissioner, when he was involved in secret plotting.

sentences.zh: 朱、馮患從榮之恣橫，嶽曾極言其禍之端，康義誠聞之不悅。

translations.literal: Zhu and Feng feared Congrong's wanton arrogance; Yue had once spoken at length of the beginnings of disaster, and Kang Yicheng heard it with displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Feng feared Congrong's arrogance; Yue had once warned at length where disaster would begin, and Kang Yicheng took offense.

sentences.zh: 及從榮敗，義誠召嶽同至河南府檢閱府藏。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, Yicheng summoned Yue to go together to the Henan prefectural office to inspect the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong fell, Yicheng summoned Yue to inspect the Henan treasury with him.

sentences.zh: 時紛擾未定，義誠密遣騎士射之，嶽走至通利坊，為騎士所害，識與不識皆痛之。

translations.literal: The turmoil was not yet settled; Yicheng secretly sent horsemen to shoot him; Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed by the horsemen—those who knew him and those who did not alike grieved.
translations.idiomatic: While disorder still reigned, Yicheng secretly sent riders to shoot him; Yue fled to Tongli Ward and was killed; all who knew him, and many who did not, mourned.

sentences.zh: 子璉，曆諸衛將軍、藩閫節度副使。

translations.literal: His son Lian served as general of the guards and military-governor deputy in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian served as guard general and military-governor deputy.

sentences.zh: 張延朗，汴州開封人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang was a native of Kaifeng in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang came from Kaifeng in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事梁，以租庸吏為鄆州糧料使。

translations.literal: He served Liang as a land-tax clerk and was grain commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as a land-tax clerk and became grain commissioner of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗克鄆州，得延朗，復以為糧料使，後徙鎮宣武、成德，以為元從孔目官。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took Yan Prefecture he obtained Yanlang and again made him grain commissioner; later when garrisons moved to Xuanwu and Chengde he was made chief clerk of the original followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took Yan he kept Yanlang as grain commissioner; later, when posted to Xuanwu and Chengde, he made him chief clerk of his original followers.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，始置三司使，拜延朗特進、工部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，兼判戶部度支事，詔以延朗充三司使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing the three-offices commissioner was first established; Yanlang was given special advancement and minister of works, made commissioner for salt, iron, and transport of all circuits, and concurrently judged revenue and expenditure of the household bureau; an edict appointed Yanlang three-offices commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing the three-offices commissioner was created; Yanlang was made special advancement minister of works, commissioner for salt, iron, and transport, and concurrent judge of household revenue; an edict named him three-offices commissioner.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，授禮部尚書，兼中書侍郎、平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was given minister of rites, concurrently vice director of the Secretariat, participant in court deliberations, and judge of the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was made minister of rites, vice director of the Secretariat, participant in deliberations, and judge of the three offices.

sentences.zh: 延朗再上表辭曰：

translations.literal: Yanlang again submitted a memorial declining, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang submitted another memorial declining, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣濫承雨露，擢處鈞衡，兼叨選部之銜，仍掌計司之重。

translations.literal: Your servant has undeservedly received imperial grace, been raised to the balance beam, and also bears the selection bureau's title while still holding the weight of the accounts office.
translations.idiomatic: I have undeservedly received imperial grace, been raised to the balance of power, and also hold the selection bureau's title while running the accounts office.

sentences.zh: 況中省文章之地，洪爐陶鑄之門，臣自揣量，何以當處。

translations.literal: Moreover the central secretariat is a place of literary composition, a great furnace and casting gate—your servant measures himself: how could he fill the post?
translations.idiomatic: The central secretariat is a forge of policy and prose; I measure myself and do not see how I can fill the post.

sentences.zh: 是以繼陳章表，疊貢情誠，乞請睿恩，免貽朝論。

translations.literal: Therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials, piled up sincere pleas, and beg imperial favor to spare court criticism.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore submitted memorial after memorial, begging your wise favor to spare me court criticism.

sentences.zh: 豈謂禦批累降，聖旨不移，決以此官，委臣非器，所以強收涕泗，勉遏怔忪，重思事上之門，細料盡忠之路。

translations.literal: Who would have thought imperial rescripts would come down repeatedly and the sacred intent would not shift—resolving on this office and entrusting your unfit servant; therefore I force back tears, strive to check my confusion, think again of the gate of serving the ruler, and weigh finely the path of utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet imperial rescripts came again and again, and your will did not change—you fixed on this office for an unfit man; so I dried my tears, steadied myself, and thought again how to serve you and remain loyal.

sentences.zh: 竊以位高則危至，寵極則謗生，君臣莫保於初終，分義難防於毀譽。

translations.literal: I reflect that when position is high, peril arrives; when favor reaches its peak, slander is born—lord and minister cannot be kept from first to last, and duty and righteousness are hard to guard against ruin and praise.
translations.idiomatic: High office brings danger; peak favor breeds slander—rulers and ministers rarely keep faith to the end, and duty is hard to defend against praise and blame.

sentences.zh: 臣若保茲重任，忘彼至公，徇情而以免是非，偷安而以固富貴，則內欺心腑，外負聖朝，何以報君父之大恩，望子孫之延慶。

translations.literal: If your servant kept this heavy charge yet forgot supreme fairness, followed private feeling to escape right and wrong, or sought ease to secure wealth and rank, then inwardly he would cheat his heart and outwardly fail the sacred court—how could he repay the great grace of ruler and father or hope for his descendants' lasting blessing?
translations.idiomatic: If I held this heavy post but forgot fairness, bent the rules for comfort, or clung to ease to keep my rank, I would cheat my own heart and fail the court—how could I repay your grace or hope for my children's blessing?

sentences.zh: 臣若但行王道，惟守國章，任人必取當才，決事須依正理，確違形勢，堅塞幸門，則可以振舉宏綱，彌縫大化，助陛下含容之澤，彰國家至理之風，然而讒邪者必起憾詞，憎嫉者寧無謗議，或慮至尊未悉，群謗難明，不更拔本尋源，便俟甘瑕受玷，臣心可忍，臣恥可消。

translations.literal: If your servant only practiced the kingly way, kept solely to state statutes, in appointing men always took the fit talent, and in deciding affairs relied on right principle, firmly opposing trends and tightly blocking doors of favor, then he could raise the great framework and mend the great transformation, aid Your Majesty's tolerant grace, and display the state's utmost reason—but slanderers and the wicked would surely raise words of resentment, and the envious would hardly lack calumny; perhaps fearing the Exalted had not fully understood, the crowd of slanders would be hard to clarify; not pulling up roots and tracing sources, one would wait to welcome flaws and accept stains—your servant's heart could bear it, his shame could be erased.
translations.idiomatic: If I only followed the kingly way, kept the laws, appointed the able, judged by right reason, and blocked favoritism, I could uphold the great order and help your tolerant rule—but slanderers would resent me, the envious would defame me, and if Your Majesty did not see the root, the calumny might stick; still, I could bear it and clear my name.

sentences.zh: 隻恐山林草澤之人，稱量聖製；

translations.literal: I only fear that men of mountains, forests, marshes, and meadows will weigh the sacred institutions;
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that recluses and common folk will judge your sacred policy;

sentences.zh: 冠履軒裳之士，輕慢朝廷。

translations.literal: and gentlemen of caps, shoes, and court robes will treat the court lightly.
translations.idiomatic: and men of rank will hold the court in contempt.

sentences.zh: 臣又以國計一司，掌其經費，利權二務，職在捃收。

translations.literal: Your servant further reflects that the state accounts office alone controls its expenditures, and the two tasks of profit and power lie in gathering revenue.
translations.idiomatic: I further reflect that the state accounts office controls expenditures, and its twin duties of profit and power lie in collection.

sentences.zh: 將欲養四海之貧民，無過薄賦；

translations.literal: To nourish the poor people of the four seas, nothing surpasses light levies;
translations.idiomatic: To support the empire's poor, nothing beats light taxes;

sentences.zh: 贍六軍之勁士，又藉豐儲。

translations.literal: to supply the six armies' stalwart soldiers again depends on full stores.
translations.idiomatic: to feed the six armies' strong soldiers again requires full granaries.

sentences.zh: 利害相隨，取與難酌，若使罄山采木，竭澤求魚，則地官之教化不行，國本之傷殘益甚，取怨黔首，是黷皇風。

translations.literal: Benefit and harm follow each other; taking and giving are hard to balance—if one exhausts mountains to harvest timber and drains marshes to catch fish, then the earthly officials' teaching will not be carried out, the state's foundation will be wounded all the more, the common people will be won to resentment, and this profanes imperial wind.
translations.idiomatic: Benefit and harm go together; giving and taking are hard to balance—if we strip the hills and drain the marshes, local government cannot teach the people, the state's root is harmed, the masses resent us, and we profane your rule.

sentences.zh: 況諸道所征賦租，雖多數額，時逢水旱，或遇蟲霜，其間則有減無添，所在又申逃係欠。

translations.literal: Moreover the levies and rents collected by the circuits, though quotas are many, often meet flood or drought, or encounter insects and frost; among them there are reductions but no additions, and everywhere they report flight, attachment, and arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the circuits' taxes, though quotas are high, often meet flood, drought, insects, or frost; collections fall rather than rise, and everywhere officials report flight and arrears.

sentences.zh: 乃至軍儲官俸，常汲汲於供須；

translations.literal: Even military stores and official salaries are constantly urgent for supply;
translations.idiomatic: Even military stores and official salaries constantly strain supply;

sentences.zh: 夏稅秋租，每懸懸於繼續。

translations.literal: summer tax and autumn rent hang ever on being continued.
translations.idiomatic: summer tax and autumn rent hang ever on the next collection.

sentences.zh: 況今內外倉庫，多是罄空；

translations.literal: Moreover now inner and outer granaries are mostly emptied;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover inner and outer granaries are now mostly empty;

sentences.zh: 遠近生民，或聞饑歉。

translations.literal: near and far the living people sometimes hear of famine and shortage.
translations.idiomatic: and people near and far report hunger.

sentences.zh: 伏惟朝廷尚添軍額，更益師徒，非時之博糴難為，異日之區分轉大。

translations.literal: I reflect that the court still adds army quotas and further increases troops and masters—untimely bulk purchase of grain is hard to accomplish, and future apportionment will grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: The court still adds army quotas and troops—emergency grain purchases are hard, and future burdens will grow.

sentences.zh: 竊慮年支有闕，國計可憂。

translations.literal: I privately fear the year's disbursement will have gaps and the state accounts are cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the year's budget will fall short and the state accounts are in peril.

sentences.zh: 望陛下節例外之破除，放諸項以儉省，不添冗食，且止新兵，務急去繁，以寬經費，減奢從儉，漸俟豐盈，則屈者知恩，叛者從化，弭兵有日，富俗可期。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will curb extraordinary abolitions, release items for thrift, not add redundant mouths, and for now stop new troops; urgently remove complexity to widen expenditures, reduce luxury and follow frugality, and gradually await abundance—then the bent will know grace, rebels will follow transformation, arms may cease one day, and a rich custom can be expected.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to cut extraordinary spending, simplify expenses, add no redundant mouths, halt new troops, strip away complexity to ease the budget, practice frugality, and wait for abundance—then the oppressed will know grace, rebels will submit, war may end, and prosperity may return.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞治民尚清，為政務易，易則煩苛並去，清則偏黨無施。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that in governing the people clarity is prized and in conducting government simplicity is prized—when simple, annoyance and harshness are both removed; when clear, partisan bias is not applied.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that governing the people favors clarity and governing the state favors simplicity—simplicity removes harsh rules, clarity ends faction.

sentences.zh: 若擇其良牧，委在正人，則境內蒸黎，必獲蘇息，官中倉庫，亦絕侵欺。

translations.literal: If one chooses good shepherds and entrusts upright men, then the common people within the borders will surely gain relief, and official granaries will also be free of encroachment and fraud.
translations.idiomatic: If we choose good governors and entrust upright men, the people within the borders will recover, and official stores will be free of theft.

sentences.zh: 伏望誡見在之處官，無乖撫俗；

translations.literal: I hope you will warn the present local officials not to depart from comforting the custom;
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to warn present local officials not to fail in comforting the people;

sentences.zh: 擇將來之蒞事，更審求賢。

translations.literal: in choosing those who will come to take office, examine more carefully and seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: and in choosing future appointees, seek the worthy with greater care.

sentences.zh: 儻一一得人，則農無所苦；

translations.literal: If one by one the right men are obtained, then farmers will have no suffering;
translations.idiomatic: If each post gets the right man, farmers will not suffer;

sentences.zh: 人人致理，則國復何憂。

translations.literal: if every man brings order, what worry remains for the state?
translations.idiomatic: if every man governs well, what worry remains for the state?

sentences.zh: 但奉公善政者，不惜重酬；

translations.literal: Only for those who serve the public with good government, do not spare heavy reward;
translations.idiomatic: Only for those who serve the public with good government should heavy reward not be spared;

sentences.zh: 昧理無功者，勿頒厚俸。

translations.literal: For those who do not understand principle and achieve no merit, do not grant thick salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Those who lack understanding and achieve nothing should not receive lavish salaries.

sentences.zh: 益彰有道，兼絕徇情。

translations.literal: Thus the Way is displayed all the more, and following private feeling is cut off together.
translations.idiomatic: This will display the Way more clearly and cut off favoritism.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下，念臣布露之前言，閔臣驚憂於後患，察臣愚直，杜彼讒邪，臣即但副天心，不防人口，庶幾萬一，仰答聖明。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will recall your servant's earlier open words, pity your servant's alarm and worry over later troubles, perceive your servant's dull uprightness, and block those slanderers and the wicked—your servant will then only accord with Heaven's heart and not guard against men's mouths, perhaps in the slightest degree to answer upward your sacred clarity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remember what I have said, pity my fear of what may follow, see my blunt honesty, and stop the slanderers—I will then follow Heaven's will and not fear men's tongues, and in some small way repay your wisdom.

sentences.zh: 末帝優詔答之，召於便殿，謂之曰：「卿所論奏，深中時病，形之切言，頗救朕失。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor answered with a gracious edict, summoned him to the informal hall, and said to him, "What you have memorialized strikes deep at the age's ailment; formed in cutting words, it has considerably remedied Our errors.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor replied graciously, summoned him to the informal hall, and said, "Your memorial strikes at the age's sickness; your blunt words have helped correct my faults.

sentences.zh: 國計事重，日得商量，無勞過慮也。

translations.literal: State accounts are weighty affairs—we can discuss them daily; do not trouble yourself with excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: State finance is weighty; we can discuss it daily—do not worry overmuch.

sentences.zh: 」延朗不得已而承命。

translations.literal: " Yanlang had no choice but to accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanlang had no choice but to accept.

sentences.zh: 延朗有心計，善理繁劇。

translations.literal: Yanlang had schemes in his heart and was skilled at managing complexity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang was shrewd and skilled at managing complex affairs.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖在太原，朝廷猜忌，不欲令有積聚，係官財貨留使之外，延朗悉遣取之，晉高祖深銜其事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate stores; apart from official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all—Gaozu of Jin deeply resented the matter.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not want him to build up stores; beyond what the commissioner left, Yanlang sent men to seize everything—Gaozu deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及晉陽起兵，末帝議親征，然亦采浮論，不能果決；

translations.literal: When troops rose at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated a personal campaign, yet also took floating opinion and could not decide firmly;
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyang rose in arms the Last Emperor debated leading the campaign himself, but listened to loose talk and could not decide;

sentences.zh: 延朗獨排眾議，請末帝北行，識者韙之。

translations.literal: Yanlang alone rejected the crowd's view and asked the Last Emperor to march north—those with insight approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang alone overruled the others and urged the Last Emperor to march north—men of judgment approved.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入洛，送台獄以誅之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent him to the metropolitan prison to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent Yanlang to prison and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 其後以選求計使，難得其人，甚追悔焉。

translations.literal: Afterward, in choosing a commissioner for accounts, it was hard to obtain the right man, and he deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when choosing a finance commissioner, no one equal could be found, and he deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 劉延朗，宋州虞城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang was a native of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang came from Yucheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 末帝鎮河中時，為鄆城馬步都虞候，後納為腹心。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was garrisoned at Hezhong he was chief inspector of horse and foot at Yancheng; later he was taken in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor held Hezhong he was chief inspector of horse and foot at Yancheng and later became a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 及鎮鳳翔，署為孔目吏。

translations.literal: When he was garrisoned at Fengxiang he was appointed chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When posted to Fengxiang he was made chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 末帝將圖起義，為捍禦之備，延朗計公私粟帛，以贍其急。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was planning to rise in revolt and made preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply the urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor planned his uprising and prepared defenses, Yanlang tallied public and private grain and cloth to meet the emergency.

sentences.zh: 及西師納降，末帝赴洛，皆無所闕焉，末帝甚賞之。

translations.literal: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking— the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the western army surrendered and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was wanting, and the emperor greatly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，除宣徽北院使，俄以劉延皓守鄴，改副樞密使，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat; soon, as Liu Yanhao guarded Ye, he was changed to vice Secretariat commissioner and rose by degrees to acting grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern Palace Secretariat bureau; soon, when Liu Yanhao held Ye, he became vice Secretariat commissioner and rose to acting grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 時房皓為樞密使，但高枕閑眠，啟奏除授，一歸延朗，由是得志。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Hao was Secretariat commissioner but only rested on a high pillow in idle sleep; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and thereby he got his will.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hao was then Secretariat commissioner but slept at ease; appointments and dismissals all passed through Yanlang, and he had his way.

sentences.zh: 凡藩侯郡牧，自外入者，必先賂延朗，後議進貢，賂厚者先居內地，賂薄者晚出邊藩，故諸將屢有怨訕，末帝不能察之。

translations.literal: For every frontier lord and prefect coming in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and only afterward discuss tribute presentation—those who bribed heavily were first placed in inner territories, those who bribed thinly went late to border commands; therefore the generals repeatedly murmured resentment, and the Last Emperor could not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Every lord or prefect coming from outside had to bribe Yanlang before tribute was discussed—heavy bribes won inner posts, light bribes meant late border assignments—so generals often complained, and the Last Emperor did not see it.

sentences.zh: 及晉高祖入洛，延朗將竄於南山，與從者數輩，過其私第，指而歎曰：「我有錢三十萬貫聚於此，不知為何人所得。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee to the southern hills; with several followers he passed his private residence, pointed, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know who will obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee to the southern hills; with a few followers he passed his house, pointed, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash here—I wonder who will get it.

sentences.zh: 」其愚暗如此。

translations.literal: " His stupidity and blindness were thus.
translations.idiomatic: " He was as foolish as that.

sentences.zh: 尋捕而殺之。

translations.literal: Soon he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon captured and killed.
